name: Qingdao
title: Qingdao Thickness Measurement for Bulk Carriers & Tankers
description: UTM in Qingdao for ore carriers, crude tankers and container ships: hull structure and hold gauging, renewal survey preparation and pre-docking checks.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Qingdao
intro: Qingdao, on the Shandong coast of the Yellow Sea, is one of northern China's main gateways for iron ore and crude oil as well as a major container port. Its ore berths and oil jetties at Dongjiakou and Huangdao receive some of the largest bulk carriers and tankers afloat. Owners use the hours after discharge, the wait for a berth and the occasional docking at Haixi Bay to find out how their holds, tanks and piping are wearing. Each Qingdao team travels from India, timed to the agent's berthing prospect.

highlights.h: Bulk carrier hold gauging after discharge
highlights.p: Once ore or coal is out and the holds are swept, a large bulk carrier waiting to sail in ballast offers open holds that can be gas-tested and entered — the best time to gauge inner bottom, hoppers, bulkheads and frames without touching cargo time.

Some coal cargoes turn corrosive with moisture and attack hold frames, brackets and lower bulkhead plating. Gauging the same grid at each Qingdao call shows whether wastage is accelerating before it reaches the substantial corrosion band.

highlights.h: From anchorage readings to a dock
highlights.p: Qingdao has its own large shipyard at Haixi Bay. Readings taken at anchorage or at a discharge berth can carry straight into a docking nearby, with one measurement plan from start to finish.

port.h: Qingdao: ore, crude and containers on the Yellow Sea
p: Qingdao's port is spread around Jiaozhou Bay and along the coast to the south-west. The Qianwan area handles containers, including an automated container terminal; the Huangdao oil port receives crude for the refineries of Shandong; and Dongjiakou, further down the coast, has deep-water berths for very large ore carriers, crude tankers and coal ships. The port is run within the Shandong Port Group, which also operates Rizhao and Yantai, and it serves one of China's most heavily industrialised provinces.

Bulk and liquid cargo set the tone for inspection. Shandong is a centre of Chinese steelmaking and of independent oil refining, so large ore carriers and VLCCs arrive laden and leave in ballast, often after waiting at anchorage for a berth. Much of that ore and coal comes from Australia, Brazil and Indonesia, so the ships here are the same Capesizes and Panamaxes seen in every major dry bulk trade. That pattern gives two different inspection windows: after discharge, when holds and ballast tanks can be opened on a ship that is otherwise idle, and during anchorage waits, when a bulk carrier in ballast can be gauged without affecting cargo operations. Coal and ore trades are hard on hold structure, and holds that have carried both for years show it in their inner bottom plating, hopper slopes and frame brackets.

Qingdao is also a shipbuilding and repair location in its own right. CSSC's Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding, in the Haixi Bay area west of the city, builds very large ore carriers and other large ships and also takes repair work, and other facilities around the bay handle smaller tonnage. For an owner whose ship trades regularly to northern China, Qingdao can be where a pre-docking survey turns into a docking, with the same thickness data carried from anchorage to dock. Container ships calling at Qianwan, by contrast, are on short mainline and intra-Asia windows, and their inspection is usually confined to deck, coamings and piping.

facilities.h: Thickness gauging in Qingdao by port area
p: Gauging in Qingdao divides by cargo. At the ore and coal berths, the team works in the holds once discharge and cleaning are done, and in ballast tanks if the ship can open them during its stay. At the oil port, tankers offer deck, external shell and piping work while discharging, with tank entry left for gas-free conditions. At the container terminals, short stays limit work to deck structure, accessible tanks and piping, and scrubber lines on ships that have them. On a tanker deck the ship's and terminal's rules on portable electrical equipment in hazardous areas govern what gauging equipment may be used and where.

Anchorage in the approaches to Qingdao is often where the most complete pre-purchase or on-hire gauging can be done, because a ship in ballast waiting for its berth has both time and access. When the ship goes into a yard — at Haixi Bay or elsewhere on the Shandong coast — we carry the measurement plan into dock, so renewal survey readings build on what has already been measured and the class surveyor sees a consistent record from the first reading to the last.
list: Dongjiakou port area — hold, hopper and inner bottom gauging on very large ore carriers and Capesizes after discharge, and deck gauging on crude tankers alongside.
Huangdao oil port — deck structure, external shell and deck and machinery-space piping gauging on VLCCs and Suezmaxes during their time alongside.
Qianwan container terminals, including the automated terminal — coaming, deck and scrubber discharge piping checks on mainline and intra-Asia container ships, fitted into tightly planned calls.
Anchorages in the Qingdao approaches — ballast-condition gauging of bulk carriers and tankers waiting for Dongjiakou or Huangdao berths, for buyers, charterers or a coming docking.
Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding, Haixi Bay — large bulk carriers in dock for renewal or docking surveys; survey gauging and re-measurement of plating after renewal.

context.h: Port state control and the northern China trades
p: Port state control at Qingdao is exercised by the China Maritime Safety Administration under the Tokyo MoU. Bulk carriers in the ore and coal trades draw attention to hold structure, hatch covers and coamings, and to the corrosion and cracking that follow years of heavy cargo handling. Scrubber-fitted bulk carriers and tankers arriving here also have China's domestic emission rules to plan for, since open-loop discharge is not allowed everywhere along the coast, and that changes how the systems are run on the approach and at anchor.

The market around Qingdao is driven by the iron ore and crude import trades and by the large ships that serve them. Owners of very large ore carriers and VLCCs want to avoid off-hire, so they favour gauging that fits inside a discharge call or an anchorage wait. Ships in the coal trade carry an extra risk, because sulphur-bearing coal and moisture together produce acidic conditions that attack hold steel. Systematic gauging of the vulnerable areas at each survey interval, rather than only at the renewal survey, shows whether wastage is accelerating before it becomes a steel renewal problem in dock.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Qingdao
jobs.p: Most ship inspection in Qingdao fits inside time the vessel already spends at a discharge berth or at anchorage. We set the scope with the superintendent before arrival, agree with the master which holds and tanks will be open, and plan the team's travel from India around the expected berthing date so the gauging starts as soon as the spaces are safe to enter.
list: Hold gauging on a very large ore carrier at Dongjiakou after discharge, covering inner bottom, hopper and transverse bulkhead plating, ahead of its renewal survey.
Tracking coal-cargo corrosion on a bulk carrier alongside in Qingdao: hold frames, brackets and lower bulkheads measured on the previous grid, with crack detection at frame end connections.
Deck and piping gauging on a VLCC discharging at the Huangdao oil port, as early preparation for a CAP survey planned at its next docking.
A buyer's thickness survey on a Panamax bulk carrier lying at Qingdao anchorage, with holds, ballast tanks and hatch covers measured and compared against the last class TM report.
Renewal survey gauging and re-gauging of renewed plating on a large bulk carrier in dock at Haixi Bay, with daily readings for the yard's steel department.

logistics: Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport is the arrival airport, usually reached through a Chinese or regional hub. The agent obtains port passes for the terminals and the oil port, where tanker berths add their own safety briefing, and arranges a launch from the port for anchorage boarding. Haixi Bay yard work needs the yard's own gate pass and induction. Visa lead time is the item that sets the plan: each technician from India needs a Chinese business visa, applied for with an invitation letter, so we ask for the berth window or dock date as early as it is known.

faqs.q: When is the best time to gauge an ore carrier calling at Qingdao?
faqs.a: After discharge, once the holds are swept and the ship is waiting to sail in ballast. That is when holds and, with the master's agreement, ballast tanks can be entered safely without interfering with cargo. If the ship waits at anchorage before berthing, part of the ballast tank programme can be done then. We plan the work around the berthing prospect the agent provides.

faqs.q: Do you check for coal cargo corrosion specifically?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships carrying coal can suffer accelerated corrosion of hold frames, frame brackets, hopper plating and the lower parts of transverse bulkheads. We gauge those areas on a consistent grid each time so readings can be compared between surveys, and add magnetic particle testing at frame end connections, where fatigue cracking tends to start once the section has thinned.

faqs.q: Can the gauging cover hatch covers and coamings?
faqs.a: Yes. Hatch cover thickness measurement is part of the renewal survey scope on bulk carriers and a frequent subject of port state control and charterer attention. We gauge cover top plates, skirt plates, coaming plating and stays, and record locations so the readings line up with the TM report. On ore carriers, coaming damage from loading equipment is noted alongside the readings.

faqs.q: Can the same team carry on into a Qingdao dock period?
faqs.a: Yes, if the timing works. When pre-docking gauging at anchorage or a berth is followed by a docking in the Qingdao area, keeping the same team means the measurement plan, the locations already recorded and the steel estimate carry straight into the dock, and the class surveyor sees one consistent set of readings rather than two.
